en: Draupnir - You came. I'm so glad Prince Rashid is safe as well.
GS - You've aged a great deal. I'm sorry. If only I had won Bifrost's support...
Draupnir - No. I was the fool. I should have been on my guard from the moment we won so easily in Cutis and Pandragon... Looking back, the Trisys campaign was reckless beyond words.
Rashid - No. At the time I don't think there was any other choice. I'm sure my sister doesn't blame you, Lord Draupnir.
Draupnir - Oh... the prince has truly grown up.
Rashid - After losing my sister and many comrades in Trisys, I wandered the desert with a man called Crow and learned a great deal. I was such a fool until then.
Draupnir - Crow?

GS - A swordsman much talked about lately, said to have conquered the Tomb of the Brave. The prince says he rescued them single-handed from the middle of the Imperial army, and afterwards travelled the desert putting the prince through all kinds of training.
Draupnir - Hmm... A mysterious swordsman indeed. I'd had reports of him, but I never imagined... Hm? Prince, where did you get the sword at your side?
Rashid - This sword? Crow gave it to me as a parting gift...
Draupnir - I can't believe it. This is the Barisada, the symbol of the master of Arondight, guardian of Pandragon. I thought it was lost with the late king in the last war...
Rashid - This is the key to Arondight?
Draupnir - Yes. You were too young to remember, but it is a royal treasure handed down together with the Three Treasures of Pandragon. To think I would see it again... Surely... the third prince...
Rashid - But how could Crow have had it?
Draupnir - It's hard to believe, but... I can think of only one explanation. You've heard of your third brother, Prince Ice, haven't you?
Rashid - Brother Ice? The finest swordsman of the house of Pandragon in a hundred years?

Draupnir - Yes. Even in a house that has produced heroes for generations, Prince Ice was famous for his talent. When the last war began he was training here in Dagal, and when he heard the news he set off for Grates at once. But by the time he arrived the battle was lost: the late king, Ashur XVII, was dead, and most of the Pandragon army had been destroyed and was in retreat. When he met the fleeing survivors, he blamed himself for arriving too late, charged alone into the enemy lines to find the king's body, and no one ever saw him again. We assume he fell then... but no one can say for sure.
GS - So Crow is Prince Ice?
Draupnir - I can't be certain. Still, for the Barisada, lost back then, to come back...
Rashid - Then can we bring Arondight back to life now?

Draupnir - It won't be easy, but I think it's possible. The first task is to repair Arondight, which hasn't moved in years. It's also important that you train so you can pilot it... But that aside, I called you and GS here for an important matter.
Rashid - What is it?

Draupnir - As you know, Pandragon has a legendary treasure handed down since ancient times: the Three Treasures, a sword, a scepter and a crown, called the holy sword Stormbringer, the Scepter of Glory and the Crown of Supremacy. Her Highness Iyolin recently won back the Scepter of Glory from the Empire, and the Crown of Supremacy, kept at Castle Pandragon, was recovered when we retook it. The problem is Stormbringer. It vanished some three hundred years ago with Yugdpain, the Adventurer King of Pandragon, while he was exploring the Eight Wonders, and it has never been found. I have long tried to learn about the Magic Tower where Yugdpain vanished, without much success, but we found a clue in the parchment brought by the man named Gishne, who arrived with GS. The Magic Isle, where the tower stands, lies in the middle of Lake Alkeonia, and its constant gales and whirlpools keep airships and ships away. But according to the parchment Yugdpain left, there is a way to reach it.
GS - What is it?

Gishne - Lake Alkeonia is so deep that its water hardly ever freezes, however cold it gets. But they say that in the coldest days of the year, from about the 1st to the 20th, the strait between the Magic Isle and nearby Wyvern Island freezes over for a while. If we use that window, I believe we can explore the Magic Tower.
Draupnir - But the Magic Tower is a place even the Adventurer King never came back from, and it will surely be perilous. That is why I called you and the prince here.
Gishne - I expect the tower holds not only the holy sword but also the statue of the god of destruction that Beradin of the Empire is after.

Draupnir - In any case, if we find the holy sword, we will have all Three Treasures of Pandragon. Then we may be able to solve the secret of the Citadel of the Sky, where the Twelve Gods are said to be sealed. In fact Yugdpain made great progress studying the Three Treasures, but when he and the holy sword vanished, the secret of the Citadel was buried with them.
GS - In any case, we'll set out for the Magic Tower right away.
Gishne - I've been studying the Eight Wonders in my own way, so I'll go with you, GS.
